## Plant breeding {.custom1}

**Traditionally**, selection is based on the phenotype, but... 

$$
P = G + E + G \times E
$$

```{r fig.height=4}
library(tidyverse)
g_main <- rnorm(50, mean = 0, sd = 1) 
g_main <- rep(g_main, times = 30)

GE_int <- matrix(rnorm(50*30, mean = 0, sd = 2), ncol = 30)
ge_int <- c(GE_int) 
gv <- g_main + ge_int

e_main <- rnorm(30, mean = 0, sd = 4) 
e_main <- rep(e_main, each = 50)

dat = data.frame(
  G = g_main, 
  GE = ge_int, 
  E = e_main
)

dat$P = dat$G + dat$E + dat$GE

ggplot(data = dat |> pivot_longer(G:P) |> 
         mutate(name = factor(name, levels = c("P","G", "E", "GE"))), aes(x = value, fill = name)) +
  facet_wrap(.~name, nrow = 1) + 
  geom_density()+
  theme_bw() + 
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.title = element_blank(), text = element_text(size = 16))

```

## Genetic markers {.custom1}

```{r echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.height=7, fig.align='center'}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggsci)

nc = c("A", "T", "G", "C")
dat = expand.grid(nc, nc)
dat$fil = ifelse(dat$Var1 == dat$Var2, NA, 1)
aa = matrix(ncol = 4, nrow = 4, dimnames = list(nc, nc))

aa[upper.tri(aa)] = 1
as.data.frame(aa) |> rownames_to_column("x") |> pivot_longer(A:C) |> 
  mutate(fil = ifelse(is.na(value),NA,paste0(x, name))) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(x, levels = nc), y = factor(name, levels = nc), 
             fill = fil)) + 
  geom_tile() + geom_text(aes(label = fil), fontface = "bold", color = "white", size = 10) +
  scale_fill_aaas() + 
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = 'none', axis.title = element_blank(),
                          text = element_text(size = 25), axis.text = element_blank(),
                          panel.grid = element_blank())
```


## Marker-assisted selection {.custom1}

::: incremental
-   Marker in [linkage disequilibrium]{.blue} with the causal genes
    -   Indirect selection
-   Higher selection intensity
-   Less time required for obtaining improved germplasm
-   Selection for traits that are hard to measure
-   Assistance in plant breeding routine procedures (backcrossing, gene pyramiding, ...)

:::

## Marker-assisted selection? {.custom1}

::: {style="font-size: 92%;"}

> "*Obviously, [the phenotype of interest needs to be unequivocally associated with the genomic region]{.underline} (i.e. the trait ↔ QTL correlation), determination of which is the focus of QTL mapping algorithms. However, even if a QTL explains 100% of the phenotypic variance for a trait of interest in a gene pool, [the QTL still needs to be unequivocally associated with the marker used to impose selection for it]{.underline} (i.e. the QTL ↔ marker correlation). [If either of these correlations (trait ↔ QTL or QTL ↔ marker) is poor, the trait ↔ marker association will not reliably improve the phenotype of interest]{.underline}, and so breeders may not only lose confidence in the value of a particular locus, but potentially in marker-assisted selection itself as an effective method.*" 
> --- @cobb_back_2019

:::

## Genomic selection {.custom1}

::: incremental
::: {style="font-size: 100%;"}
-   Most economically important traits are influenced by many genes
-   It is hard (impossible) to identify them all
-   Next-Generation Sequencing: whole genome coverage
-   [Genomic approach]{.green}: use all information available
    
:::
:::

. . .

::: {.callout-note style="font-size: 1.3em"}

The main differences between QTL mapping, genome-wide association studies and genomic selection are in the objectives (inference or prediction) and in the statistical methods used to model the genetic effects

:::

## How does it work? {.custom1}

$$
\bar{y}_i = \mu + \sum_{m=1}^p x_{im} \beta_m + \varepsilon_i
$$

-   $x_{ij} \to$ allele dosage of marker $j$ in genotype $i$

-   $\beta_j \to$ effect of marker $j$ 

. . .

::: {.callout-tip style="font-size: 1.3em;"}
If genotypes share marker alleles, and these markers are in **linkage disequilibrium** with important QTL, then one can predict the performance of unseen genotypes using marker information.
:::

## How does it work? {.custom1}

```{=html}
<div class="figure-with-source">
  <img src="C:/Users/saulo/OneDrive/Palestras/Misc/wallace.png" style="width: 78%;" />
  <div class="figure-source">
    <a href="https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30285496/" target="_blank">Wallace et al. (2018)</a>
  </div>
</div>
```

## How does it work? {.custom1}

$$
\bar{y}_i = \mu + x_{i1}\beta_1 + x_{i2}\beta_2 + \dots + x_{ip}\beta_p + \varepsilon_i
$$

. . .

::: {.callout-caution style="font-size: 1.5em;"}

## In the multiple regression setting...

Each marker would have a **fixed** value referred to its contribution to the phenotype, depending on how linked are the marker and the QTL
:::

## How does it work? {.custom1}


```{r echo=TRUE}
set.seed(55)
dat = data.frame(
  geno = paste0("G", 1:5),
  y = rnorm(5, mean = 10, sd = 2)
)
dat = cbind(dat, matrix(
  rbinom(35, size = 2, prob = .5),
  ncol = 7,
  nrow = 5,
  dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("M", 1:7))
))
dat
```

## How does it work? {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}
mod = lm(y ~ M1 + M2 + M3, data = dat)
summary(mod)
```

## How does it work? {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}
mod = lm(y ~ M1 + M2 + M3 + M4, data = dat)
summary(mod)
```

## How does it work? {.custom1}

```{r echo=TRUE}
mod = lm(y ~ M1 + M2 + M3 + M4 + M5 + M6 + M7, data = dat)
summary(mod)
```

## Population types {.custom1}

::: incremental
-   **Training population**: used to estimate the model's parameters
    -   Both phenotyped and genotyped
-   **Testing population**: used to evaluate the model's predictive ability
    -   Both phenotyped and genotyped
-   **Breeding population**: where the model will be applied
    -   Only genotyped

:::

## Population types {.custom1}

## Model evaluation {.custom1}

-   Predictive ability (PA): $\operatorname{Cor}\left(\bar{y},\hat{y}\right)$

. . .

-   Prediction accuracy (ACC): $\frac{\operatorname{Cor}\left(\bar{y},\hat{y}\right)}{\sqrt{h^2}}$

. . .

```{=html}
<div class="figure-with-source">
  <img src="C:/Users/saulo/OneDrive/Palestras/Misc//salva.png" style="width: 90%;" />
  <div class="figure-source">
    <a href="" target="_blank">Salvador Gezan</a>
  </div>
</div>
```

. . .

-   Root of mean squared prediction error: $\sqrt{\frac{1}{V}\sum^n_{i=1}(\bar{y}_i - \hat{y}_i)^2}$

-   *Instant* method: correlation within each fold
-   *Hold* method: correlation after predicting all folds
    -   More appropriate when sample size is small

## Concluding remarks {.custom1}

::: incremental
-   Genomic selection has high potential to increase plant breeding efficiency
    -   Increase selection intensity, decrease costs and generation interval
-   Inserting genomic selection into a breeding pipeline is not an easy task
    -   Which stage? 
    -   How to build a proper training population? 
    -   How to perform the selection and control the inbreeding? 
    -   How to deal with phenotypic and genomic data?
    
:::
